text:
kai: Heads-up: seeing a spike in tail latency for hosted inference in us-west-2. Dashboard shows a cluster of GPUs on rack uw2-gpua with repeated sensor flips and transient powercap events. Some pods got evicted and one inference job returned Xid 79 mid-stream. :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] 1799012345 - GPU thermal sensor flip detected on cluster-uw2-gpua (3 cards) · metric: nvml_temp_sensor_flip_count >> threshold (3m average).
jason: Any NVML logs or dmesg snippets? Can you paste the Xid details?
kai: Pasting clipped nvml & kernel snippets:```[nvml log] gpu0 temp=95C -> sensor_loss -> reported temp=0 -> driver applies powercap 150W
[driver] nvmlEvent: GPU 0: ECC single-bit corrected (count=2)
[kernel] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:81:00): 79, PID 2245, context 0x01e03
Fan RPMs: gpu0 6200 -> 0 -> 6100 (intermittent)```
maria: That's not a single-card failure pattern; looks like sensor flapping across the board. Suggest do a graceful drain of the affected nodes and move inference traffic, enable fallback models in routing policy. We should avoid automated scale-downs until we confirm stability. :thumbsup:
rene: Also check the power management firmware mismatch we saw last month — some AMP builds had a broken thermal offset. Can we confirm firmware versions with `nvidia-smi -q` and compare? If firmware mismatch + driver combo -> sensor reads can misreport and trigger powercap.
jason: Quick check command for node list and firmware: ```for n in uw2-gpua-2{1..8}; do ssh $n "nvidia-smi -q | grep -E 'GPU Current Temp|Power Readings|VBIOS Version'"; done```
oncall-sre: Starting drain: uw2-gpua-23, uw2-gpua-24 flagged for immediate cordon+drain. Migrating pods now. I'll set autoscaler min to current to prevent scale-in.
kai: Thanks. Adding that we saw Xid 31 on one pod after migration started — probably from in-flight context drop. Will watch for model corruption/regression alerts.
maria: Action items: 1) Drain flagged nodes (oncall-sre) 2) Collect full nvml logs + i2c sensor telemetry (kai) 3) Run firmware check against known-good manifest (rene) 4) Open vendor RMA if hardware shows persistent fan/tach drop (maria)
infra-bot: [ANNOTATION] Eviction count: 8 pods; avg tail latency +120ms for affected routes.
rene: If firmware/drivers look clean, let's try force-persist GPU clocks and disable auto-powercap for a short window to validate (non-production lane). Command: `nvidia-smi --auto-boost-default=0 --applications-clocks=3000,14000` (run in maintenance window only).
jason: Noted. Also saw ECC single-bit spikes — track for conversion to 2+ bit errors which would force immediate RMA. Kai, keep an eye on ECC parity counters.
kai: Uploading full logs to the incident folder: /incidents/2026-03-18/1799012345/nvml.tar.gz. I also captured a short telemetry CSV of fan RPMs and powercap timestamps.
oncall-sre: Drain complete for uw2-gpua-23, 24. No failed pod restarts post-migration so far. Keeping them cordoned for now.
maria: I'll open ticket INF-1147 with vendor and attach logs, request priority RMA if hardware shows repeated fan tach drop + sensor loss. Proposed maintenance window: tonight 02:00-04:00 PT for deeper diagnostics.
jason: +1 for window. Also rolling back recent driver update on a single node for canary test might be informative.
kai: Observed one more Xid 79 on uw2-gpua-25 after migration but it's isolated. Moving traffic off that server as well.
rene: If we confirm hardware flake, prefer to replace cards instead of repeated reboots. We saw reboots mask the issue previously and it came back 24h later.
maria: Filing RMA and escalation to vendor support. Ticket INF-1147 created. Attaching nvml logs and kernel oops. ETA from vendor expected within 48 hours.
kai: Will monitor. If anyone sees new Xid codes or ECC multi-bit, ping immediately and mark nodes OOS.
infra-bot: [RESOLVED?] Automated mitigation in place: routing fallback to smaller model variants, extra retry on generator endpoints. Keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
